context.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations in AWS eu-west-1 for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It delivers sub-50ms fraud decisions and provides a case management UI for fraud analysts.]

## Key Elements
• Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External System)
• Card Schemes / Tokenization Service (External System)
• Identity Provider (External System)
• Audit / Compliance Archive (External System)
• Real-Time Fraud Screening System (System-in-Scope)
• Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers (Users)

## Relationships
• Payment Gateway -> gRPC/HTTPS -> Real-Time Fraud Screening System (Authorization screening, R-01, R-04)
• Real-Time Fraud Screening System -> HTTPS -> Card Schemes / Tokenization Service (Tokenized card data, R-05)
• Fraud Analysts -> HTTPS/OIDC -> Real-Time Fraud Screening System (Case management & feedback loop, R-02, R-03)
• Real-Time Fraud Screening System -> AWS KMS / S3 Object Lock -> Audit / Compliance Archive (Tamper-evident logs, R-06)

## Technology Stack
• AWS ECS / AWS Lambda: Containerized microservices architecture optimized for cost and agility under a 3-engineer constraint
• AWS SageMaker / Optimized Redis Cache: High-throughput inference runtime meeting <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS (R-04)
• Amazon DynamoDB: Low-latency state management for real-time feature stores and case management
• S3 Object Lock (WORM): Cryptographically secure, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention (R-06)
• AWS KMS: Encryption at rest and cryptographic binding for explainability integrity and secure model loading (R-03, R-05)
• OAuth2 / OIDC via External IdP: Enforces strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and MFA for analysts

## Rationale
[This architecture leverages managed AWS services to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team while respecting a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Strict tokenization, circuit breakers, and immutable logging ensure PCI-DSS compliance, explainability, and high availability.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management interface for analysts. It is operated by a three-engineer team on AWS within a €25,000 monthly budget while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Payment Gateway / Acquirer**: External client sending authorization requests.
- **Identity Provider**: External system handling user authentication.
- **Audit / Compliance Archive**: Long-term tamper-evident storage destination.
- **API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy**: Java/Spring Cloud Gateway container performing TLS termination, circuit breaking, and PAN tokenization.
- **Fraud Scoring Engine**: Java / Spring Boot container executing in-memory fraud evaluation via gRPC.
- **Case Management & Rule UI**: Node.js/TypeScript container handling analyst reviews and self-service rule management.
- **Amazon DynamoDB**: Data store for rule metadata and active case states.
- **Amazon S3 with Object Lock**: Storage container with AWS IAM SCPs for 7-year tamper-evident audit logs and rule distribution.
- **Amazon SQS**: Asynchronous message broker for audit logging and rule update notifications.

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy via HTTPS/TLS 1.3.
- API Gateway to Fraud Scoring Engine via gRPC over internal VPC security groups with mTLS.
- API Gateway to Case Management Service via HTTPS/REST.
- Fraud Scoring Engine and Case Management to Amazon DynamoDB via AWS SDK.
- Fraud Scoring Engine and Case Management to Amazon S3 via HTTPS.
- Case Management Service to Amazon SQS via AWS SDK.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider**: AWS (`eu-west-1`) using Amazon ECS on Fargate for container orchestration without Kubernetes overhead.
- **Compute & Routing**: Java (Spring Cloud Gateway, Spring Boot) for low-latency processing; Node.js/TypeScript for case management.
- **Data & Storage**: Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency metadata; Amazon S3 with Object Lock for 7-year audit retention.
- **Messaging**: Amazon SQS for asynchronous decoupled messaging within budget constraints.
- **Security & Observability**: AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Amazon ECR for vulnerability scanning, and AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while easily supporting 3,000 TPS under a €25k monthly budget. In-memory fraud evaluation and isolated private subnets guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts. It operates within a mid-size payment processor to ensure secure, compliant, and low-latency transaction processing.

## Key Elements
* API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy (Java / Spring Cloud Gateway, Netty)
* Fraud Scoring Engine (Java / Spring Boot)
* Case Management & Rule UI (Node.js / TypeScript)
* Amazon DynamoDB
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock
* Amazon SQS
* AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) & AWS ECS on AWS Fargate
* AWS KMS & AWS Certificate Manager Private CA

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy: Authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
* API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Fraud evaluation requests [gRPC over internal VPC security groups with mTLS]
* API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy -> Case Management & Rule UI: Routing requests [HTTPS / REST]
* API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy -> AWS KMS: Tokenization and payload encryption [HTTPS / AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
* Java / Spring Cloud Gateway with Netty: Ensures non-blocking reactive routing for high-throughput concurrency.
* gRPC: Provides low-latency, serialized internal communication within the AWS VPC.
* AWS ECS on Fargate: Minimizes infrastructure management overhead for a three-engineer team.
* Amazon DynamoDB: Delivers low-latency storage for real-time case management and session data.
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Stores immutable 7-year audit logs in compliance with regulatory mandates.

## Rationale
This architecture uses cloud-native AWS services and lightweight reactive components to maintain sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly bounds PCI-DSS scope through early tokenization and ensures resilience via automated fail-open mechanisms.

Fraud Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Fraud Scoring Engine screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time to detect fraud while supporting analyst case reviews. It balances strict PCI-DSS compliance, explainability, and sub-50ms latency within a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- **API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy**: Java with Spring Cloud Gateway
- **Fraud Scoring Engine (Container)**: Java with Spring Boot, deployed on AWS ECS (Fargate)
- **Decision Orchestrator Component**: Spring Bean coordinating the request lifecycle
- **Feature Aggregator Component**: Java with Caffeine Cache
- **Rule Evaluation Component**: Drools / Java with DRL rule hot-reloading from local disk
- **Model Scoring Component**: ONNX Runtime for Java with local ONNX model hot-reloading
- **Decision Explanation Assembler Component**: Merges rule triggers and feature importance vectors
- **Audit Payload Assembler Component**: Appends cryptographic HMAC via AWS KMS
- **External Storage & Messaging**: Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon S3 with Object Lock, Amazon SQS

## Relationships
- **API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy -> Fraud Scoring Engine**: Fraud evaluation requests via gRPC over internal VPC security groups with mTLS
- **Decision Orchestrator -> Feature Aggregator, Rule Evaluation, Model Scoring**: In-process concurrent method calls
- **Decision Orchestrator -> Decision Explanation Assembler -> Audit Payload Assembler**: In-process method calls
- **Audit Payload Assembler -> Amazon SQS**: Asynchronous audit payload emission using AWS SDK
- **Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon S3**: Secure model and rule artifact synchronization via HTTPS with cryptographic SHA-256 signature verification

## Technology Stack
- **Java / Spring Boot / Spring Cloud Gateway**: Core language and framework for scalable microservices and API routing.
- **gRPC**: Low-latency communication protocol for internal service-to-service requests.
- **Drools**: Rule engine for executing compiled decision tables in memory.
- **ONNX Runtime for Java**: Lightweight machine learning model execution directly in native memory.
- **Caffeine Cache**: High-performance in-memory caching for low-latency feature aggregation.
- **AWS ECS (Fargate)**: Container orchestration with auto-scaling to support a three-engineer team limit.
- **Amazon S3 with Object Lock & Amazon DynamoDB**: Tamper-evident, long-term audit storage and metadata persistence.
- **AWS KMS**: Cryptographic key management for HMAC signing and encryption-at-rest.

## Rationale
This architecture uses in-memory execution (ONNX and Drools) and non-blocking asynchronous auditing via SQS to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a 25k EUR budget. Strict cryptographic signing, mTLS, and AWS KMS integration ensure PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

Case Management & Rule UI.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management & Rule UI system enables fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions and risk managers to update fraud rules without downtime. It operates within a secure AWS cloud infrastructure while maintaining strict PCI-DSS compliance.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers
* External Identity Provider
* API Router / BFF (Node.js / Express / tRPC)
* Case Management Service Component
* Rule Authoring & Validation Engine
* Audit Dispatcher Component
* Serverless Sandbox & Audit Lambda Functions
* Amazon DynamoDB
* Amazon SQS
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
* Identity Provider -> API Router / BFF: User authentication [OIDC / HTTPS]
* Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers -> API Router / BFF: Analyst reviews and rule management [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
* Case Management Service -> Amazon DynamoDB: Reads and writes active case states [AWS SDK / TCP]
* Rule Authoring & Validation Engine -> Amazon SQS: Publishes validated rules [AWS SDK]
* Audit Dispatcher -> Amazon SQS: Forwards sanitized audit events [AWS SDK]
* Amazon SQS -> Serverless Audit Lambda: Asynchronous log processing [AWS Lambda Event Source]
* Serverless Audit Lambda -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Writes immutable audit logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Node.js with TypeScript and Express/tRPC: Selected for the BFF and services to maximize development velocity for a 3-engineer team.
* Amazon DynamoDB: Chosen for low-latency active case state storage and real-time SLA metrics.
* Amazon SQS: Utilized for decoupled, asynchronous ingestion of rule updates and audit logs to prevent container blocking.
* AWS Lambda: Deployed for serverless execution of rule sandboxing and audit log persistence to minimize infrastructure management and IAM attack surface.
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Implemented to provide tamper-evident, 7-year audit log retention for compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture balances stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability requirements with the resource constraints of a three-engineer team. Leveraging serverless components (AWS Lambda, SQS, S3 Object Lock) offloads operational overhead while guaranteeing high availability and tamper-proof compliance logging within budget.

Amazon SQS.analysis:
## Overview
This system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present authorizations and supports fraud case management. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance while meeting sub-50ms latency targets on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers (Users)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer and Card Schemes / Tokenization Service (External Systems)
- API Gateway & Tokenization Proxy (Java / Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Java / Spring Boot)
- Case Management & Rule UI (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- Amazon SQS (Standard Queues with DLQs)
- Identity Provider and Audit / Compliance Archive

## Relationships
- Case Management & Rule UI -> Amazon SQS: Dispatches rule updates and audit logs asynchronously [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Amazon SQS -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Delivers rule update notifications [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Persists transaction states and idempotency records [AWS SDK]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon S3: Stores tamper-evident audit logs via downstream workers [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring managed scalability within budget constraints
- Amazon SQS (Standard Queues): Asynchronous message broker providing high throughput for rule updates and audit logging without blocking low-latency paths
- AWS KMS: Customer Managed Keys (CMK) enforcing encryption at rest for PCI-DSS compliance
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident storage satisfying the 7-year auditability requirement

## Rationale
This architecture uses SQS Standard queues to decouple high-throughput audit logging from the critical payment path, guaranteeing sub-50ms P99 latency. Fully managed AWS services minimize operational overhead, fitting within the 3-engineer team capacity and fixed monthly budget.
